reason: Phagocytes are shown engulfing debris near the cut, making them a plausible first part of wound repair.
expectation: The phagocytes will clear debris from the wound.

effect: The wound is cleared of debris and now has supply, surface and support slots to fill.
reaction: The named slots make the next stages clearer.
reason: Repair signals are shown acting on the nearby vessel, suggesting they can establish a wound supply.
expectation: The signals will help the capillary supply the healing wound.

effect: The signals produced a new vessel branch that remains connected to circulation, suggesting it can fill the wound's supply slot.
reaction: The picture makes the new branch's connection clear.
reason: The capillary sprout appears to provide the supply the healing wound needs.
expectation: The sprout will fill the wound's supply slot.

effect: The capillary sprout fills the supply slot and forms a blood-flow route that can nourish developing tissue.
reaction: The connected loop makes the supply role clear.
reason: Fibroblasts need raw materials to build the wound's supporting tissue.
expectation: The fibroblasts will produce a supporting matrix for the wound.

effect: Fibroblasts used the nutrients to make new connective tissue, which appears suited to the support slot.
reaction: The collagen fibres make the support role clear.
reason: The new connective tissue can support the damaged dermis.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the wound's support slot.

effect: The new connective tissue fills the support slot, but the result explains that the young tissue is still weaker than uninjured skin.
reaction: The distinction between closing the wound and regaining strength is useful.
reason: The epidermal edge cells need nutrients and appear suited to rebuilding the wound surface.
expectation: The nourished edge cells will form new surface tissue for the wound.

effect: The nourished edge cells formed a new surface that appears ready to fill the remaining slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes the surface repair clear.
reason: The new epidermal surface should close the wound.
expectation: The new surface will fill the surface slot and close the wound.

effect: The new surface completed the wound-closing goal, while the deeper tissue still needs to gain strength. The remaining goal is to clear the clot.
reaction: It is useful to see that the surface can close before the deeper tissue regains strength.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, so they appear suited to removing the temporary clot.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary fibrin clot.

effect: The clot-clearing enzymes completed the remaining goal. The skin is closed, but the scar and its collagen are still maturing.
reaction: The distinction between clearing the temporary clot and continuing tissue repair was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the new surface was most worthwhile because it showed that cells can span the gap while deeper tissue is still gaining strength.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and fitting the new surface felt somewhat repetitive: the two actions separated preparation from placement, though the picture explained what the cells did.

surprise.text: The capillary sprout joined another vessel to form a local flow route, making the supply role more concrete than simply adding a vessel.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The named slots and picture descriptions made the choices clear, although combining cells directly with nutrients simplified the underlying processes.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it developed these connections further. The distinction between a closed wound and a still-maturing scar gave the sequence a useful outcome.
